## Design of experiments for life sciences

FielDHub is a free, open-source R package and Shiny app for the design of
experiments. It randomizes field, greenhouse and laboratory experiments:
completely randomized (CRD), randomized complete block (RCBD), Latin square,
factorial, split-plot, split-split-plot and strip-plot designs; square,
rectangular and alpha lattices, incomplete block and row-column designs; and the
unreplicated, augmented, partially replicated (p-rep) and sparse designs used in
plant breeding and multi-location trials. It serves agriculture, plant breeding,
forestry, and animal and biological sciences.

Every design comes with a field map and a field book. Every design in the app is
also an R function with the same arguments, so a script can reproduce what the
app made.

## What's new in 1.7.5

- **Design-aware trait simulation.** `stats::simulate(x)` generates trait data
  for all 21 field designs using their treatment and experimental units.
- **Optional spatial correlation.** Simulate field variation on physical
  row and column coordinates. The Shiny app uses the same simulator for
  tables, heatmaps, and downloads.

## What's new in 1.7.0

- **A new design.** `augmented_row_column()` builds augmented row-column
  designs, in which every check appears once in every row or every column of
  the field. It has its own page in the app under Unreplicated Designs.
- **One style for every field map.** One muted colour per replication or block,
  white alleys between them, grey lines around incomplete blocks, a white grid
  around every plot, and one muted colour per check.
- **Better partially replicated designs.** An optional rule keeps the copies of
  an entry in distinct rows and columns (`rowcol_penalty`), and the spreading
  optimizer is much faster.
- **A refreshed app.** New Welcome, Help and About pages: the Welcome page
  links to every design, and Help gives each design its guide, reference page
  and offline `help()` command.

See the [release notes](NEWS.md) for every change, including the changes to
results for a given seed.

## Installation

From CRAN:

``` r
install.packages("FielDHub")
```

The development version, from GitHub:

``` r
remotes::install_github("DidierMurilloF/FielDHub")
```

## Launch the app

``` r
library(FielDHub)
run_app()
```

The app's dependencies install with the package, and it needs Shiny 1.8.1 or
newer. To keep other sessions responsive while a long design runs, install
`mirai` and start the app with `run_app(workers = 2L)`. Workers need an
installed FielDHub; without `mirai`, or when running from the package source,
designs run in the app's own session.

## Designs

FielDHub has `r length(FielDHub:::fieldhub_app_registry())` designs, grouped as
in the app's menus. Each links to its reference page.

```{r designs, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
registry <- FielDHub:::fieldhub_app_registry()
group <- vapply(registry, `[[`, character(1), "group")
label <- sub("^New - ", "", vapply(registry, `[[`, character(1), "label"))
engine <- vapply(registry, `[[`, character(1), "engine")
designs <- data.frame(
  Menu = ifelse(duplicated(group), "", group),
  Design = label,
  `R function` = sprintf("[`%s()`](https://didiermurillof.github.io/FielDHub/reference/%s.html)", engine, engine),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(designs)
```

## What you get

- **A field map** of every location, ready for reports.
- **A field book** with plot numbers, rows, columns and entries, to download
  and load into a database or field app.
- **Simulated data.** The app can simulate a response variable along with the
  randomization, for teaching and for testing an analysis before the season.
- **A reproducible record.** `write_design()` saves a design or a standalone
  replay script, `read_design()` reads it back, and `reproduce_design()`
  rebuilds it from its recorded inputs and seed.

## Example: a multiple diagonal arrangement

A project needs to test 280 genotypes in a field of 16 rows and 20 columns,
split among three experiments. Four checks are placed on diagonals across the
experiments and fill 40 plots, 12.5% of the field. To get the same design in
the app and in a script, use the same seed, here 1249.

```{r}
diagonal <- diagonal_arrangement(
  nrows = 16,
  ncols = 20,
  lines = 280,
  checks = 4,
  plotNumber = 101,
  splitBy = "row",
  seed = 1249,
  kindExpt = "DBUDC",
  blocks = c(100, 100, 80),
  exptName = c("Expt1", "Expt2", "Expt3")
)
```

A summary of the design:

```{r}
print(diagonal)
```

The first 12 rows of the field book:

```{r}
head(diagonal$fieldBook, 12)
```

The field map. Each check has its own muted colour and appears throughout the
field; the grey lines mark where each experiment starts and ends.

```{r diagonal-map, fig.align='center', fig.width=9, fig.height=6, fig.alt='Field map of the multiple diagonal arrangement: entry numbers on light grey plots, four checks in muted colours along diagonals, and grey lines between the three experiments.'}
plot(diagonal)
```

The same field by experiment:

```{r diagonal-experiments, fig.align='center', fig.width=9, fig.height=6, fig.alt='Field map of the three experiments, each on its own light background and labelled by name.'}
plot(diagonal, text.string = "EXPT")
```

In the app you can also choose how many filler plots to add and where. The R
function adds fillers only when the experiments do not fill the field.

More examples are in the
[diagonal arrangement article](https://didiermurillof.github.io/FielDHub/articles/diagonal_arrangement.html).

## Example: a partially replicated design

Partially replicated (p-rep) designs are common in early-generation trials:
some entries are replicated and the rest appear once. Here 75 entries appear
twice and 138 entries once, in a field of 16 rows and 18 columns (288 plots),
with seed 77.

```{r}
pREP <- partially_replicated(
  nrows = 16,
  ncols = 18,
  repGens = c(138, 75),
  repUnits = c(1, 2),
  planter = "serpentine",
  plotNumber = 1,
  exptName = "ExptA",
  locationNames = "FARGO",
  seed = 77
)
```

A summary of the design:

```{r}
print(pREP)
```

The first 12 rows of the field book:

```{r}
head(pREP$fieldBook, 12)
```

The field map. Replicated entries are on soft blue and the rest on light grey.

```{r prep-map, fig.align='center', fig.width=9, fig.height=7.4, fig.alt='Field map of the p-rep design: entry numbers in a white grid, replicated entries on soft blue and unreplicated entries on light grey.'}
plot(pREP)
```

More examples are in the
[partially replicated article](https://didiermurillof.github.io/FielDHub/articles/partially_replicated.html).

## For teaching

FielDHub is used in courses on statistics, experimental design and plant
breeding. Students see the randomization, the field layout and the data in one
place; simulated responses give them a data set to analyse from the first
class; and because every design is an R function with a seed, an assignment
can give each student the same randomization, or a different one.

## Documentation and help

- The [FielDHub website](https://didiermurillof.github.io/FielDHub/) has a
  guide for every design, worked examples and the function reference.
- In R, `help("diagonal_arrangement", package = "FielDHub")` and the other help
  pages work offline.
- [Video tutorials](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC4i3oTcU58Za42DbWwqF9Kg)
  walk through the app.
- Found a bug or missing a design?
  [Open an issue](https://github.com/DidierMurilloF/FielDHub/issues).
